Consolidating and integrating social protection

For funding that is more effective and reaches the right households

Arief Anshory Yusuf ·
Dewan Ekonomi Nasional · Universitas Padjadjaran

Jakarta, 14 October 2026

Part 1

The money and the target

Rp508 trillion a year, and a poverty target that needs the fall to come three times faster

Part 1 · The money and the target

Indonesia spends less on social assistance than its peers, and more on energy subsidies

0.7%
of GDP on social assistance in Indonesia
Against 2.2% in East Asia and Pacific and 2.0% in upper-middle-income countries
1.7–2.0%
of GDP on energy subsidies and compensation
Two to three times the social assistance budget, weakly targeted and moving with world prices
3x
peers spend on social assistance, as a share of GDP, compared with Indonesia
Labour market programmes and pensions are also smaller in Indonesia than in either comparison group

Indonesia spends less on social assistance than its peers and more on energy subsidies. The question for Satu Dana is how to move money between the two, and how to make each rupiah reach the right household.

Source & method
World Bank, 360 Targeting Review of Social Assistance (forthcoming), slide 6, ASPIRE 2024. Social assistance covers non-contributory schemes: conditional and unconditional cash transfers, in-kind aid, social pensions, public works, and fee waivers for health and education. Energy subsidies and compensation: 1.7 to 2% of GDP, same source.

Part 1 · The money and the target

Rp508 trillion a year, but more than half is price subsidies

277 T
of the Rp508 T total is price subsidies
Energy, fertiliser and non-energy: 55%. No recipient is recorded by name.
0.7%

Peer countries spend about 2.0%. Energy subsidies and compensation take 1.7–2.0% of GDP.
1.0–1.2
points a year needed to reach 4.5–5.0% by 2029
Poverty was 8.07% in March 2026. It fell 0.40 points in the last year. The Gini ratio rose to 0.368.

The money is large. Most of it is not attached to a named household, and the part that is still spreads thin.

Source & method
Nota Keuangan RAPBN 2026 (components as reported, August 2025); grouping by the author. Energy subsidy with compensation is Rp356.8 T (Subsidi Scoping, DEN, July 2026). GDP shares: World Bank, 360° Targeting Review, August 2026, ASPIRE 2024. Poverty and Gini: BPS, March 2026. Required pace: (8.07 minus target) over three survey years.

Who receives it, who does not, and why

Three of four target households do not receive PKH or Kartu Sembako. Four in ten recipients are outside the target group. September 2025 is the first round after DTSEN came into use in June 2025, and the errors did not move.

Source & method
Susenas March and September 2025 (BPS), processed by DEN. Exclusion error: share of the target group that does not receive the programme. Inclusion error: share of recipients outside the target group. Deciles of per capita spending, national. The September question covers receipt over one year, the March question over four months. PBI is asked in March only. The same series runs from March 2023 with no change (Digitalisasi Bansos, DEN, 10 Sep 2026). Kemensos reports lower errors from its own DTSEN-based measurement; the two methods are not comparable, which is itself a reason for one agreed measure.

Part 2 · Why the money misses

Energy subsidies: the benefit follows consumption, not need

24.6%
of BBM compensation goes to the richest decile
The poorest decile gets 3.4%. Susenas March 2025.
Flat
LPG 3 kg benefit: about the same in every decile
Each decile receives about 7–12% of the benefit: wide access, no targeting.
12.6%
of electricity subsidy recipients are in decile 1
They receive 6.9% of the benefit. The benefit rises with the decile.

A price subsidy pays more to whoever consumes more. The same rupiah paid to a named household in the bottom deciles lowers poverty and inequality at once.

Source & method
Left: World Bank, 360 Targeting Review of Social Assistance (forthcoming), slide 6, ASPIRE 2024 from Susenas March 2023, all energy subsidies combined. Right: DEN staff calculation from Susenas March 2025 (DEN policy summary 2026, slide 22; Subsidi Scoping, July 2026): electricity subsidy and compensation for 450 and 900 VA, Pertalite compensation, LPG 3 kg subsidy.

Part 2 · Why the money misses

Why the money misses: quota, process and classification

Three causes, and only the first can be fixed by a funding decision.

1. Quota smaller than the eligible group The bottom 40% is 26 million households; the budget covers 10 million for PKH and 18.3 million for Sembako. Whoever ranks first gets in; the rest are counted as exclusion error.
2. Slow, inconsistent process Nomination by village meetings that rarely happen, verification by many offices. In Banyuwangi one Sembako applicant waited 10 months for the card.
3. Wrong decile DTSEN deciles come from a 2022 census and a 39-variable formula. Household conditions change within months.

Source & method
Quota table: World Bank, 360 Targeting Review of Social Assistance (forthcoming), slides 42 and 44, Susenas March 2025 and MoSA quotas. PMT accuracy: DEN replication of the BPS PMT, November 2025 (Digitalisasi Bansos, DEN, 10 Sep 2026, annex): the formula estimated on Susenas 2023–2024 and tested on 2025. Banyuwangi: World Bank, 360 Targeting Review of Social Assistance (forthcoming), slide 40. Changing the database alone does not remove these causes.

No formula is error-free where most work is informal. The countries that hold accuracy publish the error, keep the registry current, and merge programmes once they share one registry.

Integration, consolidation and Satu Dana

One registry and one channel first; fewer, larger benefits next

Part 3 · Integration, consolidation and Satu Dana

Integration: one dynamic registry, one short formula, one payment channel

4.46 jt
families registered on the Portal by 9 September 2026
160,058 agents; 258 districts so far
514
districts from October 2026
National rollout mandated by the President, 20 July 2026
16 pts
lower inclusion error with the lean formula
25–26% against 41.5% for the current machine-learning formula
1
Register
The household applies on the Perlinsos Portal, alone or with an agent
2
Verify
Answers checked against Dukcapil, PLN, BPJS, Korlantas, ATR/BPN through SPLP
3
Update
DTSEN becomes dynamic: the decile is recomputed from current data
4
Rank
A short formula of 8–9 verifiable variables
5
Decide and appeal
Eligibility for every programme from one record; complaints change the record
6
Pay
Every cash benefit to an account in the recipient's name

Integration means one process for every programme, from registration to payment. The budget authority of each ministry does not change.

Source & method
Chart: World Bank, 360 Targeting Review of Social Assistance (forthcoming), slides 27 and 36–37, Susenas March 2022–2025; the lean formula uses household size, electricity, phone and internet spending, car, computer, land, floor area and location. DEN's parallel 8-variable model gives 26.0% (DEN and World Bank, 2025). Rollout: DEN policy summary 2026, slide 27. Process: DEN theory of change for DPI in social protection.

Part 3 · Integration, consolidation and Satu Dana

Evidence from the Bali pilot: exclusion falls, inclusion only with a dynamic registry

BPNT in Bali, March 2025 basisBefore the pilotWith the DTSEN decile as appliedWith a dynamic DTSEN decile
Exclusion error (desil 1–4 not receiving)87.6%63.5%63.0%
Inclusion error (recipients in desil 5–10)51.2%47.1% not significant25.2%
Coverage (share of all households)5.3%15.5%11.2%

Exclusion error fell by 24 points because coverage tripled. Inclusion error falls only when the decile is recomputed from current data. If the quota does not follow eligibility, exclusion error cannot fall.

Source & method
Tim Pensasaran KPTDP, evaluation of the DPI pilot for BPNT in Bali (draft for comments, 2026). 6,127 Susenas households in Bali linked to the pilot data; actual decile from Susenas March 2025; the pilot treated as if run in March 2025. The dynamic-decile column recomputes the decile from the household's current answers and is an upper bound. Confidence intervals cover sampling only. Internal evaluation, preliminary.

Part 3 · Integration, consolidation and Satu Dana

Consolidation: one family benefit, not one account

19 jt
households covered
About 65% of eligible households, at no extra budget
Rp47 T → 31 T
cost of inclusion error, PKH + Sembako + PIP
Whole system: Rp77 T to Rp44 T
Rp1.5 T → 0.7 T
a year in data collection cost
On-demand registration instead of a census every few years

Consolidation means merging PKH, Kartu Sembako and PIP into one family benefit with one targeting rule and one payment, as Brazil merged four transfers into Bolsa Família in 2003. Not one account: each ministry keeps its budget.

Source & method
World Bank, 360 Targeting Review of Social Assistance (forthcoming), slides 48 and 50, Susenas March 2025 simulation: a unified transfer with the lean formula, benefit about 15% of the poorest quintile's consumption, inclusion error about 30%, exclusion error about 35%. Brazil: Lei 10.836/2004, Cadastro Único.

Part 3 · Integration, consolidation and Satu Dana

Impact: poverty falls 2.4 points with uniform rules, 0.5 points if delivery stays fragmented

Retargeting with uniform rules across programmes cuts poverty by 2.4 points. The same retargeting with each programme keeping its own rules cuts it by 0.5. The effect on the Gini ratio is small in both cases: social assistance is too small to move inequality much, which is why the energy subsidies matter.

Source & method
World Bank, 360 Targeting Review of Social Assistance (forthcoming), slide 50, microsimulation on Susenas March 2025 with the lean PMT. Uniform rules: one targeting rule for all programmes, overlap allowed among the poorest households. These are simulated results; the review notes that actual results depend on implementation quality.

Part 3 · Integration, consolidation and Satu Dana

Energy subsidies: from price support to support for named households, as the RPJMN already requires

Element of the reform from 2027Where it is mandated
Eligibility set by DTSEN plus commodity criteria, not by owning a meter, a vehicle or a cylinderInpres 4/2025: DTSEN as the single data source
A capped cash benefit per eligible household for a reference level of consumptionRPJMN 2025–2029: from commodity subsidies to beneficiary-based support
Prices move gradually towards economic cost, without sudden shocksNota Keuangan RAPBN 2026: gradual change, subject to data and infrastructure readiness
Delivery through DPI: the same registry, eligibility and payment channel as bansosThe 2026 pilot and the national rollout from October 2026

The shift is already government policy. For Satu Dana the question is only whether the largest perlinsos item is inside its scope.

Source & method
Budget: Nota Keuangan RAPBN 2026 (Subsidi Scoping, DEN, July 2026, slide 2). Mandates and reform elements: the same deck, slides 5–8. ESDM and Pertamina are not in this meeting; the point here is scope, not the price path.

Part 3 · Integration, consolidation and Satu Dana

Five decisions for Satu Dana

DecisionWhat it meansWhen
1. ScopePillar 1 of Satu Dana covers all social protection spending, including energy and fertiliser subsidies and the KUR interest subsidy.This meeting
2. One measureExclusion and inclusion error of every programme, computed every year by BPS with one method (Susenas matched to DTSEN) and published.Integration stage, 2026–2027
3. Payment records by NIK, across programmesEvery social protection payment is recorded with the recipient's NIK and joined across programmes, so overlap and households that receive nothing can be seen. Budget tagging marks the money; records by NIK show who receives it.Integration stage, 2026–2027
4. Quota follows eligibilityThe number of recipients is set from DTSEN eligibility, not the reverse. Satu Dana is where this trade-off is decided.Budget cycle 2027
5. First five programmesPKH, Kartu Sembako, PIP, PBI JKN and BLT Desa as the five programmes the roadmap integrates first, on one registry and one payment channel.Roadmap target: 5 programmes by 2028

Decisions 1 to 3 change no ministry’s budget authority and can be agreed today.

Source & method
Stages and targets from the Peta Jalan Satu Dana (BP Taskin, 2026): regulation 2027–2028, 5 cross-ministry programmes integrated in 2028, 10 in 2029, 20% then more than 50% of the budget identified in Satu Dana.
